checks.name: a9-the-memory-adapter-has-no-second-envelope
checks.summary: internal/store/memory/source_guard_test.go parses every *.go file in the package with go/parser, fails outright on a zero-file scan, and asserts by AST and literal scan that no struct field, struct tag, constant, variable, type, function name or string literal in the package names or carries record_schema under any spelling (normalisation is lowercase with underscores and hyphens removed, so RecordSchema, record_schema, recordSchema, RECORD_SCHEMA and record-schema are all one entry). Measured result logged by the test: scanned files=2 (excluded source_guard_test.go, which necessarily spells the forbidden name and is asserted to be the ONLY exclusion) structs=4 fields=21 declared-identifiers=81 string-literals=69; no record envelope exists in this package. Matcher controls recorded: five known-positive spellings all normalise to the forbidden name; four known-negatives (schema, Requirement, recordSchemaVersionOfSomethingElse, requirements) do not. WHY THIS IS THE CHECKABLE FORM OF THE BOTH-STORES REQUIREMENT: internal/store/memory holds typed Go values in maps and has no serialization boundary, so it has no envelope field, no envelope constant and no comparison to widen. Copying internal/store/firestore's predicate here would create a SECOND envelope implementation carrying a rule with no data to apply it to, and two implementations are how two adapters come to disagree. The requirement's real content is that there is exactly ONE envelope implementation in the repository, and this guard is what keeps that true: if this adapter ever gains a serialization boundary the test fails and forces the author to route it through RecordSchemaAccepted. verdict: PASS. neither internal/store/memory/store.go nor internal/store/memory/store_test.go was edited -- both are byte-identical to the base tree.
